question.text: Once the benchmarking agency (e.g., CRISIL, NSE, or Preqin for IVCA-notified agencies) issues the Benchmark Report to Nilgiri Multi-Strategy Fund (Cat III), what is the Manager's disclosure obligation under SEBI's framework?

answer.text: Only the Trustee needs to see the Benchmark Report; no investor disclosure is required
Disclosure is optional until the fund exceeds INR 500 crore in AUM
Disclose only if the fund has beaten the benchmark; underperformance may be suppressed
Disclose the benchmarked performance in all marketing materials and investor reports

explanation.text: The Logic: Per Section 8.8.1: 'AIFs would be required to disclose the benchmarked performance, as derived by the Benchmarking Agency, in all marketing materials and investor reports.' This enables LPs to compare apples-to-apples across funds in the same Category with similar strategies. Underperformance cannot be suppressed; selective disclosure would violate the circular. The Trap: Option A is wrong — disclosure is to investors, not just the Trustee. Option C is a 'survivorship/self-reporting' trap — precisely the bias SEBI's rule is designed to prevent. Option B fabricates an AUM threshold that doesn't exist in the framework. Cross-Exam Context: XIX-B (Cat III Distributor) tests this from the disclosure-to-client angle. XIX-C / XIX-D test the Manager's disclosure obligation. Selective-disclosure prohibition is a common thread. Manager's Pro-Tip: Automate the benchmark-disclosure refresh in your investor-reporting template — each half-year, pull the latest Benchmark Report values and embed them in the investor letter, fact-sheet, and website. A stale benchmark disclosure is a SEBI-inspection red-flag.
